min_stable_gain.source: p1 Features; p2 Table 4 (device comparison); p25 Section 9.2.2.2
min_stable_gain.below_min_gain: p25: 'decompensated and requires a high-frequency gain of 7 V/V or greater to be stable. Using the OPA855 in lower gains results in increased peaking and potential instability.' p18 Section 8.3.3: about 62 deg phase margin at noise gain 7 V/V; second A_OL pole occurs before 0 dB crossing so phase margin < 0 deg at gain 1 (unstable). p15 Section 7: inverting -7 V/V with 50-ohm matched termination has noise gain 5.3 V/V and shows 5 dB peaking (Fig 6-1). For TIA: noise gain flattens at 1 + C_TOT/C_F (Eq. 2, p25), C_TOT = photodetector C + amplifier CM and differential input C; decompensated amplifiers are suitable because the TIA high-frequency noise gain exceeds 0 dB (p18).

tia_content.bandwidth: Eq. 2 (p25): high-frequency noise gain = 1 + C_TOT/C_F. Eq. 3 (p30): noise gain = 1 + Z_F/Z_IN. Bandwidth depends on C_IN (PD + CM + diff + stray), GBWP and R_F (p22)

application_guidance: TIA layout (p29-p30): cut power/ground planes under signal I/O pins; if required C_F < 0.15 pF use two series resistors of R_F/2 to reduce parasitic C; keep PD on the same PCB side; add R_ISO = 10-20 ohm close to IN- to damp trace-inductance resonance with an APD; close the R_F, C_F, R_ISO loop near the APD pins; trim TO-can leads. Use FB pin for R_F (Fig 8-4). Bias-cancellation resistor on IN+ may be bypassed with 1 uF (p16). Connect PD to VS+ to enable (Fig 9-12). Decompensated amplifier suits TIA because high-frequency noise gain > 1 (p18). Dc bias at IN+ sets output headroom; output swings toward VS- for an APD sourcing current into the loop (p22).
abs_max_and_input_protection: VS 5.5 V; V_IN (VS-) - 0.5 V to (VS+) + 0.5 V; differential input 1 V; continuous input current +/-10 mA; continuous output current +/-100 mA; TJ 150 C; TA -40..125 C; Tstg -65..150 C (p5). ESD HBM +/-1500 V, CDM +/-1500 V (p5). Internal ESD diodes to both supplies on all pins and two anti-parallel diodes between the inputs (p17 Fig 8-3). In power-down, a differential input above one diode drop opens a low-impedance path from IN+ to OUT (p20).
other_notes: Power down (p7, p20): disable threshold 0.65 min / 1 typ V and enable threshold 1.5 typ / 1.8 max V, referenced to VS-; PD bias current 70 typ / 140 max uA; turn-on 15 ns, turn-off 120 ns. Text p20 gives thresholds for 3.3 V single (0.65 / 1.8 V), +/-1.65 V (-1 / 0.15 V) and +/-2.5 V (-1.85 / -0.7 V) supplies; hysteresis designed in.
Capacitive load (Fig 6-5, Fig 6-21, p8/p11): recommended series R_S 16.5 ohm for 10 pF, 8 ohm for 47 pF, 5.6 ohm for 100 pF, 1.6 ohm for 1 nF.
Closed-loop response: Fig 6-2 shows nearly identical small-signal response at 5 V and 3.3 V supply; Fig 6-3 load 100/200/400 ohm (p8).

Inconsistencies: (1) phase margin text 62 deg vs about 74 deg from Fig 6-10; (2) A_OL table 76 dB typ vs about 80 dB on Fig 6-10; (3) SSBW table 2.5 GHz vs about 3.1 GHz on Fig 6-1; (4) LSBW table 850 MHz vs about 0.95 GHz on Figs 6-6/6-8; (5) 0.1-dB flatness table 200 MHz vs about 440 MHz on Fig 6-7; (6) current noise table 2.5 pA/rtHz at 1 MHz vs 2.84 on Fig 6-11; (7) e_n at 10 MHz, 25 C: 0.965 (Fig 6-12) vs 0.99 (Fig 6-11) vs 0.98 table; (8) Fig 9-3 legend says C_F (and 'I_RN, R_F = 2.5 pF') but text says C_PD; (9) Fig 6-15/6-16 legends say 'VOUT = 100 ohm' instead of R_L; (10) Fig 6-37/6-38 y-axis labelled mV, values are V; (11) Section 9.2.1.2 says 'ADC54J64' and 'OPA855-Q1/OPA859-Q1' for the Fig 9-1 parts; (12) symbol e_i used for current noise.
Fig 6-1 inverting -7 V/V peaking: text (p15) says 5 dB; curve reads about 4.3 dB.
Histograms (p14, 13780 units): V_OS mean -0.2 mV sigma 0.15 mV; I_OS mean 0.04 uA sigma 0.1 uA.
